# User guide: Agent Store

## In plain words

The Agent Store is the page where you install, upgrade and set up the AI agents. It shows one card for each agent. A card tells you which version is installed, whether a newer version exists, and what the agent starts with. You can keep the agent on a release channel, pick one exact version, roll back to an older version, or remove the agent. You can also set the secrets, environment variables, launch arguments and terminal defaults that every workspace of that agent starts with. An upgrade does not have to stop your running workspaces. A running workspace keeps the version it started with until you move it.

## Where to find it

1. Open **Settings** in the Unraid WebGUI.
2. Open **AI CLI Agents**.
3. Press the **Agent Store** tab.

Expect: a page called **AI Agent Marketplace** with a search box, the filters **All**, **Installed** and **Updates**, and one card for each agent.

At the top right of the page you see the button **Check for updates** and a status line next to it. The status line is described in "Check for updates" below.

## The agents

The plugin offers 15 agents. Each card has a header row with the agent icon, the agent name and one line of status, such as "v2.1.302 · update 2.1.307 available" or "Not installed". The (i) button in the header opens the short description, the **Release notes** link when the vendor publishes release notes, the install method and the package name.

| Agent | Installed from | Sign-in and keys |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Claude Code | npm (the Node package registry) | Type `/login` in the agent on first launch. The login stays in your home across reboots and upgrades. |
| Gemini CLI | npm | Run `gemini auth login` on first launch. You sign in with your Google account. |
| Codex CLI | npm | Run `codex login` (browser sign-in), or add `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the **Variables** panel. |
| OpenCode | npm | The **Variables** panel shows one API key field. |
| OpenCode 2 | npm (the package `@opencode/cli`) | The **Variables** panel shows one API key field. You can also sign in inside the agent. |
| Kilo Code | npm | The **Variables** panel shows one API key field. |
| Pi Coder | npm | The **Variables** panel shows one API key field. |
| GitHub Copilot | npm | The **Variables** panel shows one API key field. |
| Factory CLI | npm | The **Variables** panel shows one API key field. |
| NanoCoder | npm | The **Variables** panel shows one API key field. |
| Qwen Code | npm | The **Variables** panel shows a **DashScope API Key** field. This is the key for the Alibaba Qwen service. |
| Goose | GitHub release | The **Variables** panel shows **Provider**, **Model** and **API Key**. You choose the provider from a list. The key is saved under the name that fits the provider. |
| Antigravity CLI | The vendor install script | On first launch the agent prints a Google address. Open it in a browser, approve the access, and paste the code into the terminal. |
| Grok Build | The vendor install script | Follow the account-linking steps inside the agent. As an option, add **xAI API Key** in the **Variables** panel. |
| Kimi Code | The vendor install script | The agent can already know your account. If it asks, use the login option inside the running agent. |

Notes on this table:

- The plugin does not ship a sign-in note for OpenCode, OpenCode 2, Kilo Code, Pi Coder, GitHub Copilot, Factory CLI or NanoCoder. Use the API key field, or follow the agent's own documentation for other ways to sign in.
- Codex CLI runs without an operating-system sandbox on Unraid. The sandbox does not work on the Unraid root file system. Codex still asks you to approve its commands.
- The first-run setup guide lists the sign-in note of each installed agent. You can read the same notes again on this page.
- The sign-in is a one-time step for each agent. The login is kept in the home of the Unraid user, not in the agent files, so an upgrade does not remove it.

### OpenCode and OpenCode 2

OpenCode 2 is the new version of OpenCode. It is a second agent, not an update of the first one. You can install both and use both at the same time.

OpenCode 2 is not in the version list of the **OpenCode** card. It has its own card, **OpenCode 2**, below it. The **Version** panel of the **OpenCode** card has a link to that card.

- OpenCode 2 keeps its own data. Its sessions, its login, its settings and its MCP servers are separate from OpenCode. OpenCode 2 never reads or changes the data of OpenCode.
- Each workspace of OpenCode 2 starts its own private server. The plugin adds this for you.
- The Config Hub can project your instructions, skills, commands and MCP servers to OpenCode 2. See [Config Hub](config-hub.md).

To use a folder with OpenCode 2 in place of OpenCode:

1. Install **OpenCode 2** on the Agent Store.
2. Close the OpenCode workspace of the folder. Press **New Workspace**, select the tile **OpenCode 2** in the section **Agent**, and select the same folder.
3. Sign in inside the agent, or add the API key in the **Variables** panel of **OpenCode 2**.

Expect: the workspace starts a new OpenCode 2 session. The old sessions of OpenCode stay in OpenCode and do not open in OpenCode 2. To go back, start the folder with the tile **OpenCode** again.

Limits: OpenCode 2 sees only the instructions, skills and commands that the Config Hub projects. Tools that the agent starts can find their own settings files (for example `~/.config/git`) in a different place, because OpenCode 2 uses its own config folder. Git still reads `~/.gitconfig`.

## How to use it

### Find an agent

1. Type in the search box to filter the cards by name.
2. Press **All**, **Installed** or **Updates** to show all cards, only the installed agents, or only the agents that have a newer version on their channel.
3. Press the sort button to change the card order between A to Z and Z to A. The page remembers your choice in this browser.

### Close, open and move the cards

Each card has a header row. Press the name of the agent (or the arrow before it) to close the card to its header row. Press it again to open the card. A closed card still shows the versions in its header and its buttons.

1. Press the **...** (more) button of a card.
2. Choose **Move up**, **Move down**, **Move to top**, **Collapse all** or **Expand all**.
3. Press **Reset layout** in the filter bar to show the cards A to Z again and open all cards.

The page remembers the order and the open cards in this browser only. A card that installs opens itself. On a desktop you can also drag the **...** button. On a phone the header buttons of an agent show icons only.

### Install an agent

1. Find the card of an agent that shows "Not installed" in its status line.
2. Press **Version** on the card if you want a channel or version other than the default. A card that is not installed has only this chip active. The other chips are grey until the agent is installed.
3. Press **Install** in the header of the card.

Expect: the card opens itself if it was closed, and a progress bar replaces the chips. When the install ends, the page reloads and the card shows the installed version and its chips.

When the agent has nothing to decide, for example no open workspace, the install starts at once. There is no confirm box.

### Check for updates

The status line next to **Check for updates** always tells you where the version numbers come from.

| Status line | What it means |
| :-- | :-- |
| Checked 3 h ago | The cards show the result of an earlier check. The line turns orange when the result is more than one hour old. |
| Checking online for new versions… | A check is starting. The button is grey until it ends. |
| Checking Kimi Code (15 of 15), with an orange bar | A check is running. The line names the agent it checks now and how far the check has got. The Activity tray shows the same line. |
| Checked just now | The check you started has ended. |
| Check failed for 2 agents: (reason) · last good check 1 h ago | The plugin could not reach the source of 2 agents. The cards keep the last good result. The line shows the first reason. |
| Versions not checked yet | No check has run on this server. |

1. Press **Check for updates**.
2. Watch the status line.

Expect: the cards refresh by themselves when the check ends. If a check is already running, for example one the page started in the background, your click follows that check to its end.

The plugin also checks on a schedule. When the check finds a newer version of an installed agent, the plugin posts an Unraid notification with the agent name and the version. A pinned agent gets no notification.

### Upgrade an agent

The header of a card always shows the version you run in full, for example **v1.4.4**. An agent with a newer version on its channel also shows the new version next to it, with an up arrow, for example **v1.5.0**. A version number is never cut: the name of the agent is cut first.

On a computer with a mouse, the **Upgrade** button shows when you point at the card or move the keyboard focus into its header. On a phone or a tablet there is no pointing. There, the new version is the button, and it is at least 44 pixels high. The **...** menu of the card also has **Update to v1.5.0…** and **Release notes**.

1. Press the new version (or **Upgrade**, or **Update to v1.5.0…** in the **...** menu, or pick a newer version in the version picker). Expect: a dialog called **Update <agent>** opens.
2. Read the two versions and the channel at the top. Under **What is new**, read the release notes. Each version has its own part; the newest one is open. When the plugin has no notes for the agent, the dialog says so and shows a link to the notes on the vendor's site. When the plugin could not load the notes, the dialog says "The release notes could not be loaded now" and shows the same link; open the dialog again later to try again. Pre-release versions are not listed.
3. Read **Your open workspaces**. It says what happens to them. The next sections describe it.
4. Decide on **Keep a copy**. The section "Keep a copy before an upgrade" describes it.
5. Press **Update now**. Press **Close** (or Escape) to leave without a change.

If another browser tab already started the update, the dialog says "An update of this agent is already running" and **Update now** is grey.

The line **Channel** names the channel. **Pick another version or channel** closes the dialog and opens the **Version** panel of the card.

Expect: the dialog closes. The card shows a progress bar and a status line in the place of the chips, and its height does not change. The header reads **Installing v1.5.0…**. When the upgrade ends, the page reloads.

When the channel offers an older version than the one you run (for example after you move from Beta to Stable), the header shows the older version with a down arrow. The dialog is then called **Change <agent> to vX** and its button is **Change version**.

The status line says what the plugin does now. When it closes workspaces, it reads "Closing workspace 2 of 3...". Then it saves your workspace data and reads, for example, "Saving workspace data (home root), 42 % done, 3 min so far...". The bar moves with the percentage. A save can take several minutes. If the percentage does not move for two minutes, the line adds "The save is slow. It is still working." The Activity tray shows the same line.

### Pick an exact version

The **Version** chip opens a panel with the release channel and a list of versions. The list shows each version as `v1.2.3`, with the tags of the vendor, for example `[latest]`. The installed version ends with `(installed)`.

1. Press **Version** on the card.
2. Open the list of versions and pick a version.

Expect: the plugin opens the confirm box at once. A newer version is an **Upgrade**. An older version is a **Downgrade**. The same version is a **Reinstall**. Choosing a version never changes the channel.

The list hides versions that are built for other systems, such as Windows, macOS or ARM processors, because they cannot run on Unraid. On the **Stable** channel the list hides alpha, beta, canary, nightly and release-candidate builds. When no version fits the channel, the list says "No versions available on this channel".

### Release channels

| Channel | What you get | When to use it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Stable** (default) | The tested release of the vendor. | Most people. |
| **Beta** | Newer releases that may be less tested. Only agents from npm, from GitHub releases and from an install script that has a GitHub address show this choice. The list shows at most the 8 newest builds. A daily build shows only its newest copy, and a build older than the current stable release is not shown. | You want new features early. |
| **Pinned** | One version, locked. The agent never changes until you pick another version. | You need the same version every day, or a newer version broke something. |

Choose a channel with its radio button. The version list then refreshes for the new channel. When you press **Pinned**, the plugin pins the version that is installed at that time. If the agent is not installed, the plugin asks you to choose an installed version first.

If the plugin cannot save the channel, it puts the old choice back and shows an error.

## How an upgrade treats your running workspaces

An agent is installed in its own layer (a read-only compressed block of files). A new version goes into a second layer next to the first. The plugin keeps at most two versions of one agent running at the same time.

### The normal case: side by side

When the new version can go beside the old one, the box says: "Installs alongside the version you are running — your N open workspaces are not interrupted, and keep the version they have until you switch them over."

- Nothing stops. Terminals stay as they are. No workspace shows "upgrading".
- There is no list of workspaces and no option to stop them.
- The button says **Install** when workspaces are open, and **Upgrade** when none are open.
- A new workspace, and a workspace that you close and open again, starts on the newest version.

When the install ends, a box says that the agent is installed and that your open workspaces still run the old version. Press **Got it**.

### Move a running workspace to the new version

A running workspace keeps its version. To move it:

1. Open the **...** menu of the workspace.
2. Choose **Switch to** (the version number).
3. Read the box. Press **Switch**.

Expect: the plugin closes the agent in that workspace, starts it again on the installed version, and resumes the same conversation. The plugin does not send "continue". You type the next instruction yourself.

> [!WARNING]
> **Switch** stops the work in progress in that workspace. Text that you typed and did not send is lost. The workspace keeps its name, folder, settings, position and Relay identity.

The menu entry appears only for a running workspace whose version differs from the installed version. This is also true after you roll a channel back, when the installed version is older. A stopped workspace needs no switch. It starts on the installed version the next time it starts.

### An old version that no workspace uses

An old version that no workspace uses does not stop an upgrade. When two versions are installed and only one is in use, the update box says: "The oldest version, v2.1.310, is no longer used by any workspace. It will be removed to make room for this update." Press **Update now**. The plugin removes that old version when the new version starts.

### When the upgrade must wait

Sometimes the new version cannot go beside the old one. Examples are two versions that open workspaces still use, a storage method without versioned activation, or an earlier upgrade that waits to go live. Then the box shows:

- **Why this upgrade must wait:** and the reason.
- "N active sessions will remain running" and the list of the workspaces (folder and short id).
- "The upgrade will queue safely and start after all sessions close naturally."
- A check box: "Force now: terminate these sessions; background subagents, monitors, and shell tasks will stop."

The confirm button says **Queue upgrade safely**. If you tick the check box, it says **Force upgrade now**.

- **Queue upgrade safely** starts nothing yet. Your workspaces keep running. The upgrade starts when the last workspace of that agent closes.
- **Force upgrade now** saves the place of each workspace, closes them, installs, and starts the same workspaces again. Each one resumes where it left off. An agent that cannot resume starts fresh. If a workspace does not come back, open it from **+ New Workspace** and press **Resume**.

> [!WARNING]
> **Force upgrade now** ends background helpers, monitors and shell tasks that run inside those workspaces. Save your work first. The plugin keeps each workspace and its saved place.

### Cancel a queued upgrade

While an upgrade waits, the status line on the card reads "Upgrade queued safely — waiting for active sessions to close". A **Cancel** button sits next to it.

1. Press **Cancel**.

Expect: the status line goes away, the buttons return, and the upgrade does not start when the workspaces close.

If the upgrade has already started, the plugin shows "Could not cancel". An upgrade that is replacing files cannot be cancelled.

### Keep a copy before an upgrade

The dialog for an update has a check box: "Keep a copy of the current version so you can roll back if the upgrade goes wrong." The box is not ticked by default.

1. Tick the check box.
2. Open **Where the copy goes**. Read the line under it. It shows a folder. You can change it. The path must start with `/`.
3. Read the sizes: the current version, the space the upgrade needs, and the free space at the folder. The estimate includes 10 percent extra space.

If there is not enough space, if the path is not valid, or if the agent has no saved installation to copy, the box tells you and turns the check box off. You can still upgrade without a copy.

If the copy fails while the upgrade runs, the plugin stops the upgrade. The installed version stays as it was. The status line reads "Backup failed — upgrade aborted (current version intact)".

### The progress card

While an agent installs or upgrades, its card shows a progress bar and a status line in the place of the chips. The card keeps the same height. An open settings panel stays where it is, dimmed, until the install ends. **Remove old versions** and **Uninstall** are grey until then. If you reload the page, the card shows the install again.

| Status line | What it means |
| :-- | :-- |
| Preparing installation… | The install starts. |
| Queueing safely — active sessions will keep running… | The upgrade waits for the workspaces. A **Cancel** button shows. |
| Installing alongside your running version… | A side-by-side install runs. |
| Closing N active sessions… | A forced upgrade saves and closes the workspaces. |
| Backing up current version… | The plugin copies the current version to your folder. |
| Queued — waiting for another agent upgrade to finish... | Installs run one at a time. |
| Upgrade queued — saving workspace data first… | The plugin saves the home before it replaces the agent. This wait can take several minutes. |
| Waiting for running processes before activating… | Programs that still use the old version hold it. The card lists them under the line, with details of each program. |
| Finalizing... | The install ends. The page reloads. |

Only the agent that waits shows a waiting line. Cards of other agents show nothing. The Activity tray also lists the install (see [Health, Activity and troubleshooting](health-and-troubleshooting.md)).

If an install fails, a box called **Failed** shows the reason. The card also keeps the reason in the place of the chips, with the buttons **Retry** and **Dismiss**. **Retry** starts the install again. **Dismiss** puts the chips back.

## Roll back

You have three ways to go back.

1. **Pick an older version.** Open the **Version** panel, choose an older version in the list of versions, and confirm **Downgrade**. The plugin installs that version again from the vendor source. It needs the vendor source to still offer it.
2. **Restore a kept copy.** If you ticked "Keep a copy" at an upgrade, the **Version** list has a group called **Restore a kept backup**. Each entry reads like `v1.0.0 — kept 2026-10-01 14:30 UTC (180 MB)`. Choose one and confirm **Restore**. The plugin first keeps a copy of the current version, so you can undo the restore. A kept copy stays available even when the vendor offers no versions.
3. **Pin the version.** Press **Pinned** to stop the next upgrade.

Antigravity CLI is the case where the kept copy matters most. The vendor serves only the latest version, so a kept copy is the only way back.

The plugin does not delete kept copies by itself. They use space in your storage folder.

## Remove old versions

The foot of an installed agent card has a link, **Remove old versions**. It frees space on the boot disk. The link says how much: **Remove old versions (frees 12 MB)**. The number counts only the older versions. The version you use stays and is not counted.

The link shows only when there is something to remove. When every old version is still in use by a workspace, the foot reads **Old versions in use** instead. When the plugin has not measured the sizes yet, the link shows with no number. While a measurement runs, it reads **(measuring…)**. The numbers change by themselves after a removal, after an install and after **Measure now** on the **Storage** tab.

1. Press **Remove old versions** on the card. Expect: a dialog lists the old versions, the space the removal frees, and the versions that stay because a workspace uses them.
2. Press **Remove**. Expect: a second dialog says how much space you got back.

The action removes old version folders, old storage layers and kept rollback copies. A version that a running workspace uses stays, and the dialog names the workspace. After the removal you cannot roll back to a removed version. The setting **Keep the previous agent version** in the **Configuration** tab decides whether the plugin keeps the last version by itself. See [Home and agent storage](storage.md).

## Uninstall

**Uninstall** is a link in the foot of the card, next to **Remove old versions**. It says how much it frees: **Uninstall (frees 92 MB)**. That number counts the version you use, the old versions and the kept copies, because they all go. The link turns red when you point at it.

1. Press **Uninstall** on the card.
2. Read "This removes the agent, all its versions and its kept copies, and frees 92 MB on the disk. Its workspaces close and leave the list. Your variables and secrets for it stay."
3. Press **Uninstall**.

Expect: the card shows **Uninstalled**, the page reloads, and the agent shows as available again.

If a process still uses the agent, the plugin removes nothing and says "The <agent> agent is still in use. Close its sessions, then try again." Close the sessions of that agent, then press **Uninstall** again.

> [!WARNING]
> **Uninstall** ends the open workspaces of that agent. It removes every installed version of the agent, the writable layers of the agent, and the kept copies in your storage folder. A kept copy that you saved to another folder stays there, and the version list still shows it.

The plugin keeps the other agents and every layer of your homes. Your login, history and memory live in the home, so they stay. You can install the agent again later.

## Choices and settings

### The chips on a card

An installed card has five chips. Press a chip to open its panel. Press it again to close it. One panel is open at a time.

| Chip | What it holds |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Version** | The release channel and the list of versions. |
| **Variables** | The secrets and environment variables that every workspace of this agent gets at launch. |
| **Storage** | The memory limit for Node agents, and the storage figures. |
| **Terminal** | The tmux defaults for this agent, and the auto-launch switch. |
| **Start options** | The launch arguments for this agent. |

A chip shows a small coloured dot when it holds something. On **Variables**, an amber dot means that a key field has no value. A green dot means that all key fields have values. A cyan dot means that you added your own variables or secrets. On **Terminal** and **Start options**, a cyan dot means that you changed the default.

### Secrets and environment variables (Variables)

The **Variables** panel sets what the plugin passes to the agent each time it starts. It has three parts.

| Part | What it is | Stored |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| The key fields at the top (for example **API Key**) | The keys the agent needs. Each agent has its own fields. | In the secrets file of the plugin, with owner-only access. |
| **Variables** | Your own environment variables, as `NAME = value` rows. The values show as plain text. | In the home. |
| **Secrets** | Your own secrets, as `NAME = value` rows. The values are masked. | In the secrets file of the plugin, with owner-only access. |

To add a row:

1. Press **Add variable** or **Add secret**.
2. Type the name. The page changes the name to capital letters and removes characters that are not letters, digits or `_`.
3. Type the value.
4. Press **Save** in that part.

To remove a row, press the trash icon and press **Save**.

For a masked value:

- A value that was saved shows as dots. Leave the dots as they are to keep the value.
- Clear the field and press **Save** to delete the value.
- Type a new value to replace it.

**The eye icon.** When you type a value in a masked field, an eye icon shows at its edge. Press it to see what you typed. Press it again to hide it. The eye only changes how the field looks. It does not save anything and it does not ask the server for the stored value. A stored value shows only as dots, and there is no eye until you type something.

**Two levels.** Every setting has two levels.

| Level | Where you set it | Effect |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Agent default | This **Variables** panel | Every workspace of the agent gets it. |
| Workspace override | The **...** menu of a workspace, **Session settings**, tab **ENV** | Only that workspace. A workspace value wins over the agent default for the same name. |

In the workspace tab, a row that differs from the agent default carries the mark **● ws**. The trash icon on such a row sets it back to the agent value. The secrets level works the same way.

Two more facts:

- The plugin stores each secret once, by its name. A key such as `OPENAI_API_KEY` reaches every agent that reads that name. Your own secrets also show in the **Variables** panel of every agent.
- Some agents show a note about a data folder variable. Gemini CLI and Codex CLI are two examples. If you set that variable to a folder outside the plugin home, the history and logins of the agent are lost at the next reboot. Leave it empty.

**Saving, and the "Restart them now" notice.** A save never restarts a workspace by itself. A running workspace keeps the old values until it restarts.

1. Press **Save**.
2. Look at the notice at the bottom of the page. It reads like "Saved. 2 running sessions use the old values until they restart." It shows only when workspaces of this agent are running.
3. Press **Restart them now** to restart, or **Close** to do nothing.
4. In the box **Restart sessions?**, read the list. Each workspace shows as **idle** or **busy**.
5. Press **Restart idle sessions**.

Expect: each idle workspace stops the agent and starts it again with the new values.

A busy workspace is never restarted from here. The list says "kept running; restart it yourself when it is idle". A workspace counts as busy when its terminal showed input or output in the last minute, or when the agent shows that it works. When the plugin cannot read the state, it counts the workspace as busy. The plugin also refuses to restart a workspace while an install of that agent runs.

### Start options

The **Start options** panel holds extra flags that the plugin adds to the launch command of the agent.

1. Press **Start options**.
2. Type the flags, for example `--max-turns 10`.
3. Press **Save**.

The plugin rejects the characters `;`, `|`, `&`, `` ` `` and `$`. It also rejects `>`, `<`, `(`, `)`, `*` and a word that starts with `#`, unless they sit inside quotes, and it rejects a quote that is not closed. The new arguments apply the next time the agent starts. A workspace can set its own arguments in **Session settings**. Some agents also get fixed flags from the plugin. You cannot change those.

### Terminal defaults (Terminal)

The **Terminal** panel holds the tmux defaults for this agent. tmux is the session manager that keeps a terminal alive on the server.

| Setting | What it does |
| :-- | :-- |
| status | Shows or hides the tmux status bar. |
| mouse | Turns mouse support on or off. |
| history-limit | The number of lines of scrollback for each pane. A higher number uses more memory. |
| prefix | The key that starts every tmux command. |
| base-index | The number of the first window. |
| bell-action | Which pane can raise a bell alert. |
| default-terminal | The terminal type that programs see. |
| focus-events | Passes focus events to programs such as vim. |
| allow-passthrough | Lets escape sequences pass through tmux, for inline images and links. |

Changes save by themselves after a short pause. The note at the bottom reads "Saving…" and then "Saved ✓". A dot marks each row that differs from the built-in default. Press **Reset all to built-in** to go back to the built-in values. The defaults apply every time the agent starts in any workspace. A workspace can override each field.

### Auto-launch for an agent

Below the tmux settings, the **Terminal** panel has a section called **Keep saved workspaces running**. It holds two check boxes.

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Restart all saved workspaces** | When on, all workspaces of this agent start after a server reboot. The plugin also starts a workspace again if its agent exits. The count of workspaces shows in the text. | Off | Turn it on for agents that you want to run all the time. |
| **Start fresh if no resume** | When a workspace has no saved place, it starts a new conversation. When off, such a workspace does not start. Turning off the first box also clears this box. | Off | Turn it on when you prefer a new conversation to no conversation. |

The page saves the change at once and shows "Saved ✓". The plugin also starts these workspaces again after a plugin upgrade. On a phone, the whole label next to a check box is the touch target.

### Storage

The **Storage** chip shows two things.

- **Max RAM (MB)** shows only for agents that run on Node (the npm agents). It sets the memory limit for the agent. The default is 4096. The allowed range is 512 to 65536. The page saves the value when you leave the field.
- **Storage** shows **Footprint** (disk space of the agent, with the number of layers), **In-memory** (recent changes that are not yet saved to permanent storage) and **Mount**. When there are unsaved changes, a **Consolidate** button shows the amount. Press it to queue a save.

### Storage health on a card

When the plugin finds a problem with the layers of an agent, the card shows a red tag in the corner and a repair button.

| Tag | What it means |
| :-- | :-- |
| halted | The plugin stopped mounting the agent until you decide. |
| missing layer | One layer file of the agent is gone. |
| missing | All layer files of the agent are gone. |
| corrupt | A layer file is damaged. |
| unmanaged layers, path drift, host mismatch | The layers do not match what the plugin expects. Hover over the tag to read the state. |

The repair buttons are **Restore** (copies a safe backup layer back, with no download), **Re-install** (installs the agent again to build a clean layer) and **Clear halt** (accepts the current state). Each one opens a confirm box first.

### Settings on other tabs that this page uses

| Setting | Where | What it does | Default |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Check for new agent versions** | **Configuration** tab | How often the plugin checks online for new agent versions: every 6 hours, daily at 6am, weekly on Monday at 6am, or never. | Daily at 6am |
| **Keep version check results for** | **Configuration** tab | How long past version check results are kept: 1, 3, 6 or 12 months. | 3 months |

## Agents that update themselves

Some agents try to update themselves while they run. An update that the agent does itself would bypass the Agent Store. The plugin would not know the new version, and the update would write new files into the agent layer.

The plugin turns the self-update off for these agents: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode, OpenCode 2, Kilo Code, Pi Coder, GitHub Copilot, Factory CLI, Qwen Code, Antigravity CLI, Grok Build and Kimi Code. For Gemini CLI and Qwen Code, the plugin writes the off-setting into the settings file of the agent one time. It never overwrites a choice that you made there. NanoCoder has no self-update. Goose updates only when you run its own update command yourself.

The change applies the next time the agent starts. A workspace that is already running keeps its old behaviour. You should upgrade only through the Agent Store.

## What happens behind the scenes

The plugin keeps each agent version as an immutable layer. The Agent Store builds a new layer, mounts it beside the old one, and switches the stable name to it. A running workspace holds the layer it started with. When no workspace holds an old layer, the plugin removes it. For the technical description, see C4 Component: Agent Version Management and C4 Component: Config Env Secrets.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| The versions look old, or the status line is orange. | The cards show a cached result that is more than one hour old. | Press **Check for updates**. |
| **Check failed for N agents**. | The plugin could not reach the source of those agents. | Check the network and the DNS of the server. Press **Check for updates** again. |
| The **Version** list says "No versions available on this channel". | The source offers no version for this channel, or the check has not ended. | Wait for the check, or change the channel. |
| An upgrade stays queued. | A workspace of that agent is still open and the version cannot go beside it. | Close the workspace, or press **Cancel** and upgrade later, or use the force option. |
| The bar stops at about 99 percent and lists programs. | Programs still hold the old version. | Close those programs or the workspace that runs them. The upgrade then goes on. |
| A box says "Backup failed — upgrade aborted". | The copy of the current version failed, for example because the disk was full. | Pick a folder with more space, or upgrade without a copy. The installed version is unchanged. |
| An upgrade is marked failed, but the new layer is not live yet. | The activation waits for programs that hold the old layer. | Close the workspaces of the agent. The upgrade finishes by itself. |
| An action says “Wait for the storage migration to finish before installing, removing, or upgrading agents.” | The plugin is changing how it stores agents and homes. | Wait for the migration status to finish, then try the action again. |
| After a save, a workspace still uses the old key. | A save does not restart workspaces. | Use **Restart them now**, or restart the workspace when it is idle. |
| The card shows a red tag. | The agent layers have a problem. | Press the repair button on the card. See "Storage health on a card". |
| An agent works but shows `v?`. | The agent is installed, but the plugin has not read its version yet. | Open a workspace of the agent, or press **Check for updates**. |

If the problem stays, open the **Debug Console** tab (see [Health, Activity and troubleshooting](health-and-troubleshooting.md)).
